Reasoning: Let the side length of the large square be a, and the side length of the small square be b. By the square diagonal formula, a=10/√2, b=8/√2. method.method_draft: From the image, note that Q and P lie on the same diagonal of the smaller square, because P is the center and Q is a corner. Let B be the bottom-left corner of the smaller square, which is also the bottom-right corner of the larger square. Then BQ is a diagonal of the smaller square, and QP is half of that diagonal, so QP=8/2=4. Also RB is a diagonal of the larger square, so RB=10. Since the squares are aligned on the same horizontal base, diagonal RB of the larger square slopes down at 45° while diagonal BQ of the smaller square slopes up at 45°, so RB is perpendicular to BQ. Because QP lies on BQ, RB is the perpendicular height from R to the base QP. Thus area of triangle PQR = 1/2 × QP × RB = 1/2 × 4 × 10 = 20.
